scope_note: Reading is reported at the scope actually read, not as whole-paper credit where only named sections were read. No source is asserted to prove the printed broad lemma without the hypothesis comparisons below.

sources.name: B. D. O. Anderson (1982), Reverse-time diffusion equation models
sources.integrity: 14 parsed pages; complete PDF read, including full Sections3–5 and Lemmas1–5.
sources.comparison: Sections3–4 require smooth unique marginal AND augmented joint/conditional forward density equations. Section5 uses a backward Kolmogorov equation and expressly does not identify trajectories. Those premises are not printed in the generic helper.

sources.name: U. G. Haussmann and E. Pardoux (1986), Time reversal of diffusions
sources.integrity: 1,081,383 bytes; proper PDF EOF; 18 parsed pages; fitz did not repair it. Author-host provenance located through public bibliographic locations and authenticated Internet Archive CDX capture. Complete18pages read, including full Lemma2.1 weak product proof and AppendixA.
sources.comparison: Theorem2.1 uses global spatial Lipschitz/linear-growth coefficient conditions and a weighted Sobolev density condition. Remark2.2 local replacement requires local uniform Lipschitz plus nonexplosion AND explicit derivative-flow estimate(2.25). Remark2.3 alternative still includes(2.23), nonexplosion and locally bounded distributional covariance second derivatives plus density H1. Smooth positive p supplies local Sobolev density regularity, but the printed source does not establish those coefficient bounds. The authors use a for a diffusion factor and aij for covariance; do not confuse this notation with our covariance a.

sources.name: J. Quastel (2002), Time reversal of degenerate diffusions
sources.integrity: Complete8pages read, including main weak-product Lemma2 proof and appendix. PDF locally converted using ps2pdf -dSAFER.
sources.comparison: The divergence-form theorem uses weighted coefficient derivative square-integrability(7), bounded density(8), and drift energy(9). Its energy estimates prove the extension to backward tests; they are not consequences stated in our helper.

sources.name: P. Cattiaux, G. Conforti, I. Gentil and C. Léonard, Time reversal of diffusion processes under a finite entropy condition
sources.integrity: Complete PDF42pages parsed. Read complete Sections2–3 (PDFpp9–22), including Lemmas3.6,3.9,3.15, full Theorem3.17 proof and stationary discussion, and AppendixA (PDFpp36–39). This is NOT a claim that all42pages were read.
sources.comparison: Theorem3.17(b) requires forward test-generator/carre-du-champ L1 integrability, continuous Gamma, convergence-determining algebra, and the finite-measure integration-by-parts hypothesis(3.21). These are genuine hypotheses. For our diffusion(3.21) asks for variation control of div(pa gradphi), not merely existence of its pointwise derivatives. The final(3.31)–(3.32) passage invokes PropositionA.11, which is stated in L1 difference-quotient form; no adaptation is asserted here from weak testing alone. The source is not used as an unverified black box.

sources.name: Y. Tang and H. Zhao (2024), Score-based diffusion models via stochastic differential equations: a technical tutorial
sources.reading: Complete Section2 and reverse-time Theorem2.1 discussion/proof consulted; no new whole-paper reading credit.
sources.comparison: Theorem uses suitable conditions and proof is expressly heuristic. The comments cite stronger Haussmann–Pardoux and Quastel regularity/energy conditions. This does not establish the generic helper as printed.

repository_classical_comparison.conclusion: The first defines C1,2 regularity of the solution/test itself. The second defines classical graph-continuous abstract evolution solutions. Neither defines classical divergence-form density equations to require separately jointly continuous coefficient-product derivatives. They do not supply a hidden derivative bound for this diffusion lemma.
